newsitem.title: UK: British homeless paper to help Russian counterpart.
newsitem.headline: British homeless paper to help Russian counterpart.

text.p: Staff of the Scottish edition of a newspaper sold on the streets by homeless people plan to help counterparts in St Petersburg launch a similar project under a British government aid project announced on Wednesday.

As part of the two-year scheme, people working for Na Dnye (The Depths), a paper based on a night shelter in the Russian city, will be flown to Edinburgh to observe the operations of The Big Issue (Scotland).
Up to eight Big Issue staff members, some themselves formerly homeless, will go to St Petersburg to advise on how to attract advertising, promote sales and plan finance.

The two papers are already linked. Last Christmas, the Scottish Big Issue raised 10,000 pounds ($16,500) in donations for Na Dnye. In March, co-director Mel Young and a homeless distributor, Bill Gilmour, went to St Petersburg to hand over the cash.
"We were a bit scared by what we found there," Young said.
"Once you become homeless, no matter where you are, it's horrendous. But in Russia the situation is far worse because there is no social welfare support and in the winter it's a damn sight colder."

Britain's Overseas Development Administration (ODA) is funding the exchanges between the two papers as part of its "Know-How Fund" which provides technical assistance for the countries of the former Soviet bloc.
The Scottish Big Issue plus an English equivalent employ hundreds of homeless people in cities throughout Britain as sales staff. The two have a combined circulation of around 300,000 copies a week.
